Facial Volume Harmony

Lesson 10: McKenzie Exercise

This is one of the foundational exercises of the course, designed to release tension in the back of the head, enhance the sense of neck length, and support a more stable and aligned posture.

The exercise helps reduce excess tension in the upper back and neck, improve control of head positioning, and create a greater sense of ease in the lower jaw area.

Notice how the neck has become more aligned. Results after 3 months of practice.

Starting position:

Stand with your back against a wall. Feet are parallel and placed hip-width apart.

The shoulder blades, pelvis, and back of the head make firm contact with the wall.

The spine is upright, shoulders open, and the crown of the head reaches upward.

Gently bring the lower jaw slightly forward and maintain this position throughout the exercise.

On the inhale, look upward.

On the exhale, smoothly lower the chin toward the chest, allowing the back of the neck to lengthen.

Hold this position for 1 second, then return to the starting position.

Continue the movement in a calm rhythm:

  • inhale, gaze upward
  • exhale, chin toward the chest

Perform 15–30 repetitions, moving slowly and maintaining steady, relaxed breathing.

Week 2 Training Assignment

Recommended plan:

  1. Monitor nasal breathing as often as possible (except during sleep).
  2. Stay aware of your tongue position throughout the day. You may set reminders on your phone if helpful. Try to swallow without lifting the tongue away from the upper palate.
  3. Practice the “Cobra” exercise as often and for as long as possible. It is especially convenient because it can be done during daily activities, and no one can see what is happening behind closed lips.
  4. Perform the McKenzie exercise daily.
  5. Continue manual work with the palate every day (at least for a few minutes).
  6. Keep practicing relaxation of the back of the head, jaw muscles, tongue, and upper head area.
